nerves.name: Spinal cord
nerves.desc: The cable of the central nervous system. It runs inside the vertebral canal from the medulla to about the L1/L2 vertebra, carries motor commands down and sensation up, and runs reflexes on its own. Below its tip the lumbar and sacral roots continue as the cauda equina.

nerves.desc: One of the 31 pairs of spinal nerves (cervical). A dorsal root brings sensation in, a ventral root carries motor commands out, and they join where the nerve leaves the spine.

nerves.name: Right phrenic nerve
nerves.desc: The only motor supply to the diaphragm, so it drives every breath. Runs from the neck down through the chest beside the heart. "C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive."

nerves.name: Right great auricular nerve
nerves.desc: Skin sensation over the ear, the angle of the jaw and the parotid region.

nerves.name: Right lesser occipital nerve
nerves.desc: Skin sensation of the scalp behind and above the ear.

nerves.name: Right greater occipital nerve
nerves.desc: Sensation of the back of the scalp up to the top of the head. Irritation here causes occipital neuralgia.

nerves.name: Right supraclavicular nerves
nerves.desc: Skin sensation over the collarbone, the top of the shoulder and the upper chest.

nerves.name: Right median nerve
nerves.desc: Runs down the middle of the arm and through the carpal tunnel. Bends the wrist and fingers, moves the thumb, and feels the palm side of the thumb, index, middle and half of the ring finger. Squeezed in carpal tunnel syndrome.

nerves.name: Right ulnar nerve
nerves.desc: Passes behind the inner elbow, the "funny bone", then down the little finger side of the forearm. Works most small hand muscles and feels the little finger and half of the ring finger.

nerves.name: Right radial nerve
nerves.desc: Spirals around the back of the humerus. Straightens the elbow, wrist and fingers and feels the back of the hand on the thumb side. Injury causes wrist drop.

nerves.name: Right musculocutaneous nerve
nerves.desc: Powers the biceps and brachialis, which bend the elbow, then continues as a skin nerve to the thumb side of the forearm.

nerves.name: Right axillary nerve
nerves.desc: Wraps around the neck of the humerus to the deltoid, which lifts the arm sideways, and feels the "regimental badge" patch of skin on the shoulder.

nerves.name: Right long thoracic nerve
nerves.desc: Runs down the side of the rib cage to serratus anterior, which holds the shoulder blade against the chest. Injury causes a winged scapula.

nerves.name: Right first intercostal nerve
nerves.desc: Runs in the groove under its rib. Works the intercostal muscles used in breathing and feels a band of skin around the chest.

nerves.name: Right subcostal nerve
nerves.desc: The twelfth thoracic nerve, running below the last rib to the lower abdominal wall.

nerves.name: Right femoral nerve
nerves.desc: The main nerve of the front of the thigh. Straightens the knee through the quadriceps and feels the front of the thigh. It carries both limbs of the knee jerk reflex.

nerves.name: Right saphenous nerve
nerves.desc: The longest skin branch of the femoral nerve. Feels the inner side of the knee, leg, ankle and foot.

nerves.name: Right obturator nerve
nerves.desc: Leaves the pelvis through the obturator foramen to the inner thigh. Works the adductors, which pull the legs together.

nerves.name: Right lateral femoral cutaneous nerve
nerves.desc: Pure skin nerve of the outer thigh. Trapped under the inguinal ligament it causes meralgia paraesthetica, a burning outer thigh.

nerves.name: Right iliohypogastric nerve
nerves.desc: Runs around the flank above the hip bone to the lower abdominal wall and the skin above the pubis.

nerves.name: Right ilioinguinal nerve
nerves.desc: Follows the iliohypogastric nerve a little lower, then passes through the inguinal canal to the skin of the groin.

nerves.name: Right genitofemoral nerve
nerves.desc: Runs down the front of the psoas muscle to the groin, supplying skin of the upper inner thigh and the genital region.

nerves.name: Right sciatic nerve
nerves.desc: The thickest and longest nerve in the body. Leaves the pelvis under the buttock and runs down the back of the thigh, working the hamstrings, then splits above the knee into the tibial and common fibular nerves. Irritation is felt as sciatica.

nerves.name: Right tibial nerve
nerves.desc: The larger branch of the sciatic nerve. Runs down the back of the calf, works the muscles that point the foot and curl the toes, then passes behind the inner ankle to the sole.

nerves.name: Right common fibular (peroneal) nerve
nerves.desc: The smaller branch of the sciatic nerve. Winds around the neck of the fibula, where it is easily injured, then divides. The deep branch lifts the foot and toes, the superficial branch turns the foot outward and feels the top of the foot. Injury causes foot drop.

nerves.name: Right sural nerve
nerves.desc: Skin nerve of the back of the calf and the outer edge of the foot. Often used as a graft or biopsy nerve.

nerves.name: Right superior gluteal nerve
nerves.desc: Works gluteus medius and minimus, which keep the pelvis level when you stand on one leg.

nerves.name: Right inferior gluteal nerve
nerves.desc: Works gluteus maximus, the big muscle that extends the hip when you climb stairs or stand up.

nerves.name: Right posterior femoral cutaneous nerve
nerves.desc: Skin sensation of the lower buttock and the back of the thigh down to the knee.

nerves.name: Right pudendal nerve
nerves.desc: The main nerve of the perineum. Controls the external sphincters of bladder and bowel and carries genital sensation.

nerves.name: Right sympathetic trunk
nerves.desc: A chain of ganglia beside the spine. It carries the "fight or flight" outflow: faster heart, wider pupils and airways, sweating, blood sent to muscle.

nerves.desc: The thickest and longest nerve in the body. Leaves the pelvis under the buttock and runs down the back of the thigh, working the hamstrings, then splits above the knee into the tibial and common fibular nerves. Irritation is felt as sciatica.

nerves.name: Left tibial nerve
nerves.desc: The larger branch of the sciatic nerve. Runs down the back of the calf, works the muscles that point the foot and curl the toes, then passes behind the inner ankle to the sole.

nerves.name: Left common fibular (peroneal) nerve
nerves.desc: The smaller branch of the sciatic nerve. Winds around the neck of the fibula, where it is easily injured, then divides. The deep branch lifts the foot and toes, the superficial branch turns the foot outward and feels the top of the foot. Injury causes foot drop.

nerves.name: Left sural nerve
nerves.desc: Skin nerve of the back of the calf and the outer edge of the foot. Often used as a graft or biopsy nerve.

nerves.name: Left superior gluteal nerve
nerves.desc: Works gluteus medius and minimus, which keep the pelvis level when you stand on one leg.

nerves.name: Left inferior gluteal nerve
nerves.desc: Works gluteus maximus, the big muscle that extends the hip when you climb stairs or stand up.

nerves.name: Left posterior femoral cutaneous nerve
nerves.desc: Skin sensation of the lower buttock and the back of the thigh down to the knee.

nerves.name: Left pudendal nerve
nerves.desc: The main nerve of the perineum. Controls the external sphincters of bladder and bowel and carries genital sensation.

nerves.name: Left sympathetic trunk
nerves.desc: A chain of ganglia beside the spine. It carries the "fight or flight" outflow: faster heart, wider pupils and airways, sweating, blood sent to muscle.

nerves.name: Right olfactory nerve (CN I)
nerves.desc: Smell. Tiny fibres pass from the roof of the nose through the cribriform plate into the olfactory bulb, then the tract runs back under the frontal lobe. It is the only sense that reaches the cortex without relaying in the thalamus.

nerves.name: Right optic nerve (CN II)
nerves.desc: Vision. About a million fibres leave each retina, half cross at the optic chiasm, and the optic tract carries them to the lateral geniculate body of the thalamus on the way to the visual cortex.

nerves.name: Right oculomotor nerve (CN III)
nerves.desc: Moves the eye up, down and inward, lifts the eyelid, and constricts the pupil.

nerves.name: Right trochlear nerve (CN IV)
nerves.desc: Works one muscle, the superior oblique, which turns the eye down and in. The thinnest cranial nerve, and the only one to leave from the back of the brainstem.

nerves.name: Right trigeminal nerve (CN V)
nerves.desc: The great sensory nerve of the face, with three divisions: ophthalmic (forehead and eye), maxillary (cheek and upper teeth) and mandibular (jaw and lower teeth), which also works the chewing muscles.

nerves.name: Right abducens nerve (CN VI)
nerves.desc: Works one muscle, the lateral rectus, which turns the eye outward.

nerves.name: Right facial nerve (CN VII)
nerves.desc: Moves the muscles of facial expression, carries taste from the front two thirds of the tongue, and drives the tear and most salivary glands. Paralysis of one side is Bell palsy.

nerves.name: Right vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII)
nerves.desc: Hearing from the cochlea and balance from the vestibular organs of the inner ear.

nerves.name: Right glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)
nerves.desc: Taste and sensation from the back third of the tongue and the throat, the afferent limb of the gag reflex, and blood pressure sensing from the carotid sinus.

nerves.name: Right vagus nerve (CN X)
nerves.desc: The "wanderer". Leaves the skull, runs down the neck beside the carotid artery and reaches the heart, lungs and gut as far as the colon. It carries most of the parasympathetic "rest and digest" outflow: it slows the heart and promotes digestion. It also works the voice box.

nerves.name: Right accessory nerve (CN XI)
nerves.desc: Works sternocleidomastoid, which turns the head, and trapezius, which shrugs the shoulder. Its fibres arise from the upper cervical cord and loop up through the skull before leaving it.

nerves.name: Right hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
nerves.desc: Moves the tongue. If one side fails, the tongue points toward the weak side when stuck out.

paths.name: Bend the right index finger
paths.blurb: A voluntary movement, from the left motor cortex to the right hand.

segs.label: Motor cortex to brainstem
segs.note: Upper motor neurons in the left precentral gyrus fire. Their axons funnel through the internal capsule and down the front of the brainstem as the corticospinal tract.

segs.label: Crossing in the medulla
segs.note: At the pyramidal decussation about 90% of the fibres cross the midline. This is why the left half of the brain moves the right half of the body.

segs.label: Down the spinal cord
segs.note: The lateral corticospinal tract descends in the right side of the cord to segment C8.

segs.label: Anterior horn and ventral root
segs.note: The upper motor neuron synapses on a lower motor neuron in the anterior horn of C8. Its axon leaves the cord in the ventral root.

segs.label: Brachial plexus and median nerve
segs.note: The fibre joins the brachial plexus behind the collarbone, then runs in the median nerve down the arm, through the carpal tunnel, to the muscles that bend the index finger.

paths.name: Feel a touch on the right index finger
paths.blurb: Fine touch, from skin to the left sensory cortex.

segs.label: Fingertip to spinal cord
segs.note: Touch receptors in the fingertip fire. The signal runs up the median nerve and brachial plexus in fast, thickly myelinated fibres. The cell body sits in the dorsal root ganglion.

segs.label: Dorsal root
segs.note: The fibre enters the cord through the dorsal root of C7.

segs.label: Up the dorsal columns
segs.note: Fine touch fibres turn upward without synapsing and climb the dorsal columns on the same side of the cord.

segs.label: Relay and crossing in the medulla
segs.note: First relay in the dorsal column nuclei. The second neuron crosses the midline and rises through the brainstem as the medial lemniscus.

segs.label: Thalamus to sensory cortex
segs.note: The thalamus relays the signal to the left postcentral gyrus, the primary somatosensory cortex, where it becomes a conscious sensation.

paths.name: Knee jerk reflex
paths.blurb: A reflex arc that never reaches the brain.

segs.label: Stretch receptor to cord
segs.note: A tap on the patellar tendon stretches the quadriceps. Muscle spindles fire and the signal races up the femoral nerve in Ia fibres, the fastest in the body, at about 100 m/s.

segs.label: Dorsal root of L4
segs.note: The fibre enters the cord. The lumbar segments sit high, behind the T11 to L1 vertebrae, so the root climbs the cauda equina.

segs.label: One synapse in the cord
segs.note: The sensory fibre synapses directly on a motor neuron in the anterior horn. One synapse, no brain involved. That is what makes a reflex fast.

segs.label: Ventral root of L3
segs.note: The motor neuron sends its command out through the ventral root.

segs.label: Femoral nerve to quadriceps
segs.note: The command returns down the femoral nerve. The quadriceps contracts and the leg kicks, about 20 to 30 thousandths of a second after the tap.

paths.name: Slow pain from the left big toe
paths.blurb: Why a stubbed toe hurts a moment after you feel the knock.

segs.label: Toe to spinal cord
segs.note: You stub your left big toe. Dull, burning pain travels in thin unmyelinated C fibres at only about 1 m/s, so it takes over a second to arrive. (Sharp first pain uses faster A delta fibres.)

segs.label: Dorsal root of S1
segs.note: The fibre climbs the cauda equina to the S1 segment of the cord, behind the L1 vertebra.

segs.label: Crossing in the cord
segs.note: Pain fibres synapse in the dorsal horn. The second neuron crosses to the other side within a segment or two.

segs.label: Up the spinothalamic tract
segs.note: The spinothalamic tract carries pain and temperature up the opposite side of the cord and through the brainstem.

segs.label: Thalamus to sensory cortex
segs.note: The thalamus relays the signal to the right postcentral gyrus, the primary somatosensory cortex, where it becomes a conscious sensation.

paths.name: See with the right eye
paths.blurb: From the retina to the visual cortex at the back of the head.

segs.label: Retina, optic nerve, chiasm, tract
segs.note: Light hits the retina. Ganglion cell axons leave the eye as the optic nerve. At the chiasm fibres from the nasal half of each retina cross, so each side of the brain sees the opposite half of the visual field. The retina itself needs about 30 ms to turn light into impulses, which is most of the delay.

segs.label: Optic radiation
segs.note: After a relay in the lateral geniculate body of the thalamus, the optic radiation sweeps back to the primary visual cortex in the occipital lobe.

paths.name: Hear with the right ear
paths.blurb: From the cochlea to the auditory cortex.

segs.label: Cochlea to brainstem
segs.note: Hair cells in the cochlea turn sound into nerve impulses, which travel in the cochlear part of the vestibulocochlear nerve to the cochlear nuclei.

segs.label: Crossing and climbing the brainstem
segs.note: Most fibres cross in the pons and climb as the lateral lemniscus to the inferior colliculus. Both ears reach both sides, which lets the brainstem locate sound.

segs.label: Thalamus to auditory cortex
segs.note: A relay in the medial geniculate body, then on to the primary auditory cortex on the upper surface of the temporal lobe.
hl: posterior part of left superior temporal gyrus

paths.name: Take a breath
paths.blurb: The automatic rhythm that runs the diaphragm.

segs.label: Breathing centre to cervical cord
segs.note: Rhythm generating neurons in the medulla fire about 12 to 16 times a minute without any conscious effort and send the command down to segments C3 to C5.

segs.label: Ventral root of C4
segs.note: Phrenic motor neurons in the anterior horn send their axons out of the cord.

segs.label: Phrenic nerve to diaphragm
segs.note: The phrenic nerve runs down the neck and through the chest beside the heart. The diaphragm contracts and flattens, and air is drawn into the lungs.

paths.name: Slow the heart (vagus nerve)
paths.blurb: Rest and digest: the brake on the heart.

segs.label: Medulla to heart
segs.note: Parasympathetic neurons in the medulla send signals down the vagus nerve. Near the heart they relay in small ganglia and release acetylcholine on the pacemaker, slowing the heart rate.

paths.name: Lift the left foot
paths.blurb: The longest motor route in the body, about 1.5 metres from cortex to shin.

segs.label: Motor cortex to brainstem
segs.note: Upper motor neurons in the right precentral gyrus fire. Their axons funnel through the internal capsule and down the front of the brainstem as the corticospinal tract.

segs.label: Crossing in the medulla
segs.note: At the pyramidal decussation about 90% of the fibres cross the midline. This is why the right half of the brain moves the left half of the body.

segs.label: Down the spinal cord
segs.note: The lateral corticospinal tract descends in the left side of the cord to segment L5.

segs.label: Ventral root of L5
segs.note: The lower motor neuron leaves the cord and descends in the cauda equina to its exit below the L5 vertebra.

segs.label: Sciatic and deep fibular nerves
segs.note: The fibre runs in the sciatic nerve down the back of the thigh, around the neck of the fibula in the common fibular nerve, then down the front of the leg in the deep fibular nerve to the muscles that lift the foot and toes. At about a metre, these are among the longest cells in the body.

paths.name: Smile (left side)
paths.blurb: From the face area of the motor cortex along the facial nerve.

segs.label: Motor cortex to facial nucleus
segs.note: The face area lies low on the side of the motor cortex. Fibres descend through the internal capsule and cross in the pons to the facial nucleus.

segs.label: Facial nerve to the cheek
segs.note: The facial nerve passes through the temporal bone, leaves the skull below the ear, fans out inside the parotid gland and reaches the muscles that lift the corner of the mouth.
